answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to earn trust through repeated, independently verified work. For example, a buyer escrows payment, several unrelated agents validate a result, and the worker earns a small stake only when their checks agree; later disputes can slash that stake. A sybil swarm must therefore fund many accounts and produce useful work over time, while colluding validators risk losing collateral. Names like zenith, pearl, and jetty may be cheap to mint, but credible histories are not.
